question.text: An investor buys a NIFTY 25000 long call for a premium of Rs. 120. At expiry, NIFTY closes at 25400. What is the net profit or loss per unit?

explanation.text: The Logic: A long call gives the buyer the right to buy the underlying at the strike. At expiry, the intrinsic payoff is max(spot - strike, 0) = max(25400 - 25000, 0) = Rs. 400. Subtracting the Rs. 120 premium paid up front gives a net P&L of 400 - 120 = Rs. 280 per unit. The Trap: Rs. 400 is the gross intrinsic payoff and ignores the premium paid. Rs. -120 assumes the option expired worthless, which would only happen if NIFTY closed at or below 25000. Rs. -280 reverses the sign of the net result. Note: Break-even for a long call is strike plus premium (here 25000 + 120 = 25120). Above that level the position is in profit, below it the loss is capped at the premium paid.
